{"source": {"id": "MLP-171", "title": "Bone Marrow Diseases", "url": "https://medlineplus.gov/bonemarrowdiseases.html", "content": "Bone marrow is the spongy tissue inside some of your bones, such as your hip and thigh bones. It contains stem cells . The stem cells can develop into the red blood cells that carry oxygen through your body, the white blood cells that fight infections, and the platelets that help with blood clotting. With bone marrow disease, there are problems with the stem cells or how they develop: In leukemia , a cancer of the blood, the bone marrow makes abnormal white blood cells In aplastic anemia , the bone marrow doesn't make red blood cells In myeloproliferative disorders, the bone marrow makes too many white blood cells Other diseases, such as lymphoma , can spread into the bone marrow and affect the production of blood cells Causes of bone marrow diseases include genetics and environmental factors. Tests for bone marrow diseases include blood and bone marrow tests. Treatments depend on the disorder and how severe it is. They might involve medicines, blood transfusions or a bone marrow transplant .", "groups": ["Immune System"], "source": "MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine", "language": "en"}, "candidate": {"positive_en": "In aplastic anemia, what does the bone marrow fail to make?", "positive_zh": "在再生障碍性贫血中，骨髓不能制造什么？", "evidence": "In aplastic anemia , the bone marrow doesn't make red blood cells", "expected_answer": "In aplastic anemia, the bone marrow does not make red blood cells.", "missing_en": "What exact percentage of patients with aplastic anemia need a bone marrow transplant?", "missing_reason": "The summary does not state any percentage of aplastic anemia patients needing transplant. It only says treatments depend on the disorder and severity and might involve medicines, blood transfusions, or a bone marrow transplant."}}
